steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: I'm sorry, we're not open yet. Please come back in the afternoon.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Sorry about the timing. I'm not here to buy art; I just have some questions.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: For your trouble.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: (Slips a gold coin through the crack in the door)

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: This is...

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Consider it a token of appreciation. And there's more where that came from, if you've got the information I need.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: A pleasure to meet you in the flesh, sir.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Er, ahem... what can I help you with?

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Last month, a painting that is very dear to me suffered moisture damage thanks to improper storage.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: I've heard that a very skilled restoration painter lives here, so I thought I would try my luck.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Oh... that could be tricky. She's not easy to find.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Does she live outside town? I've got more gold coins.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: (Takes out a gold coins from his sleeves)

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: No, she's in town, but she's a little eccentric. We keep our distance from her, when we can help it.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: She's got a temper? Violent type? Or more of an arrogant artist?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Well... you might say she's got a sunny disposition.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: It's not so bad when she's at home painting, other than the strange noises, from time to time. When she's sketching outside, though... everyone stays as far away as they can. Don't want to get press ganged into modeling for her.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: There's no getting away once she sets her eyes on you. You have to sit there and wait for her to finish, no matter what else you might have to do.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: And, as you know, paintings aren't the quickest thing to get done... poof, there goes your whole day.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Why don't you just say no?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Yeah... why not just turn her down? Seems easy enough.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: (Mutters to himself with a blank expression)

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Sir? Are you okay?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: I-I'm fine. I'm trying to think back to what she said to me, but I just can't remember a thing.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: That's a little weird... heh.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Anyway, it doesn't matter. She's a little loopy, you know. Says lots of weird things.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Don't let the things she says get to you. I'm sure she doesn't mean any harm by them.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Heh... didn't think you'd turn around and start defending her.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: She's a little off-kilter, sure, but she's never hurt anybody. Plus...

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Half of what I sell here is her work. Her stuff is popular.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: A hardworking painter! Now I'm even more curious.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Well, sir, if you insist, I can take you to her.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: This is where she lives. I'll be on my way now.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: You're not coming in with me?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Er... well, I have a thing.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Okay, then. Thanks.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: (Takes out a few gold coins from his sleeves)

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: For your trouble.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Oh, thank you so much! That's kind of you. Please feel free to come by my shop if there's anything else I can help with.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: Goodbye now.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Huh? Oh, alright, goodbye.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: What a nice little hideout.
It is almost noon, and the sun shines brightly outside.

Inside, however, all the doors and windows are tightly shut, with only a few rays of sunlight leaking through the cracks between the boards that have been nailed to the windows, preventing the room from being entirely engulfed in darkness.
The visitor hears the faint sound of scratching coming from the darkest corner.
He straightens his robe and approaches a massive canvas standing upright. A woman is using her brush to fill it with color.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Should the brush be drier? But then the brush marks would be too distinct...

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: No, that's not the color that I wanted.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: How's that? Does that look better?

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: The colors could run further down the canvas. I have to do it with a single stroke. No interruptions now... none whatsoever.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: It's been a while...

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Oh, it's you. Have a seat.

steps.name: Strange Outsider
steps.text: When was the last time you cleaned? You can't see anything in that mirror anymore.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Hah, are you belittling my humble abode, Father? You can't imagine the inspiration I find here.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You haven't changed a bit. You don't care about anything but your art.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You've changed a lot. Your brow didn't furrow like that.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Really...?

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Something on your mind?

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Well, if you don't want to talk about it, I won't pry.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: The first time I saw you, you were absorbed in your painting, just like this.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: The first time you saw me? When was that? It's been so long, I can't remember.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I was hiding behind that boulder, that day you met the Herald for the first time.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: So you were by the water... all I remember is the beauty the Herald showed me. I've never seen a creature so beautiful.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: The Herald must have felt your admiration, guiding you into we many after just one contact.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I've always been grateful.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: But you turned around, one step from the ocean.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I'm not making excuses.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Did you abandon the many and turn against your kin just to finish this painting?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: (Touches the canvas with a finger)

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: So beautiful, but burdened by so much sin.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: But your regret hasn't stopped your brush.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You were too stubborn, too short-sighted. You trapped yourself in the canvas and failed to see the distant future.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You didn't understand the many. You couldn't fit in with the many. You should have nourished the many if you could not be assimilated.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: That should have been your end. I am regretful, but joyful. We will become one, sister.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: (Sleeves quiver)

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Would you put that away for now? I want to finish this before it's all over.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: (Straightens sleeves)

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: It took me a long time to get here. I can wait a little longer.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: And there's something I wanted to ask you before I end your life.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Go on. My brush won't stop, though.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Why did you choose to leave us?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Life is eternal in we many. We are inextricably linked, sharing our joy, anger, sorrow, happiness.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: That 'sharing' you're talking about is just about robbing me of all emotion, transforming me into a mouth for the will of the many.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Your outbursts are meaningless. It will not soothe your anger, nor abate your sorrow. It will only make you wallow in boundless misery as you step ever closer to destruction.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: We many have sealed away excess emotion. A constant state of heightened alertness is not conductive to the many's continued survival.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You should cast it away and embrace peace and tranquility with us, free from the trappings of your own emotion.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: My cries of sorrow, anger and angst are the fertile soil of my art.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I never joined you to get peace or tranquility.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Then what did you want from us?

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: That's never changed, whether I chose to join or leave.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I want beauty, eternal beauty, dwelling in all life.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Didn't you find it?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: A glimpse of the Herald's beauty was enough to change your life forever. Was that not enough?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: The Herald left his seed in you, made you one of us, to partake in our beauty.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Yes, your bodies hold the ultimate beauty, beyond anything else.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: But have you ever noticed it, appreciated it?

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: The choices you make guide you to eternal art, but you can't even be moved by art.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You faced survival and evolution, and your answer was to abandon the concept of beauty.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: When I started to assimilate, I became numb. I couldn't create or appreciate.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You don't know how I felt when I realized that my brush was covered in dust... the pain I felt in that moment told me I had to leave the many.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: So you could not let go of human desire.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Humanity created art as a form of self-expression. Humanity admires art to seek the ego within.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Humanity is looking into a mirror, as humanity always has.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: It's selfish, and pathetic...

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: (Puts down the brush)

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You've finished.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Yes, I have.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Blue. As far as the eye can see. You've seen the depths of the ocean, and you understand that the confines of the canvas are too small for the great waves.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You saw the sea... but what I painted was a puddle.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: The destiny of water began in the ocean, and in the ocean it shall end.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: That's the destiny of water, not the ocean.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You have put your last stroke on the canvas. It's time to go.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I spent months without sleep in order to finish it. You came at just the right time. Maybe you should take another look, as the first being to lay eyes on it.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: To us, it's a piece of cloth with color on it. It has no meaning.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Cloth? No, you're wrong. You used to say that I couldn't see true greatness because I was fixated on the canvas. What about you, then?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: What?
Every surface in the room begins to peel away, revealing an eerie hue of blue beneath.
The blue begins to devour other colors around it, as though alive.
It soon takes over the entire house, even the cracks between the planks on the window, blocking out the sun completely.
The room should have turned pitch-black, but instead it is blue as far as the eye can see.
An ominous blue, a sinister blue.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Ah... so this is the big picture. Literally.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I have far underestimated the progress that you've made in the past six months.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Go home, Father. You never saw me. You missed your chance to catch me.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: What a shame...

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You shouldn't have asked so many questions. Hunting and feeding don't need words.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You shouldn't have come looking for me on your own.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Over the past few years, I have been troubled by my failure to reach the next stage of metamorphosis. I've been trying to find out why.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: After thinking on it, I still have a human desire: curiosity. That's why I wasn't able to metamorphose any further.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Looks like you stopped at the same place. A part of the human is always there with you, and you can't put it down, no matter how much you want to.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Ah... what a shame.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Leave, Father. You won't become one of them, just like I couldn't. Run away, like I did.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: *Hiss*—Not giving up?

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You won't cut any deeper than a flesh wound.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: ...Damn.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: What did you put on me?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Just a little mark.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You're far too powerful for me to purge on my own, but there will be kin who can. The mark will guide the way for them, and it will continue to beckon as long as you still draw breath.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I gave you a chance, Father.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You chose to run away. You should be prepared to run forever.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I've reached a dead end. There's no way forward for me. I shall remain on the path forever.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: My carcass will nourish those who come after me, who will go further.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: I respect your choice.
To the visitor's eyes, the blue around him begins to warp, struggling to break free.
Large lumps of slime fall to the ground and wriggle their way towards the visitor, crawling up his robes and leaving behind a wet trail.
They surround him tightly, the slime congealing into threads, then tentacles that bury him.
The last thing he sees as his vision fades away is the pitying gaze of a woman.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You think we're on the same path. But actually, our paths have only momentarily intersected.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: You thought I ran away, but actually, I've just reached a crossroads.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: The road keeps on going.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Goodbye.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Looks like I can't stay here anymore.

steps.name: Eccentric Artist
steps.text: Where could I work undisturbed?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: What was that sound?

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: You heard it too? I came to see what's going on.

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: Hey, is that a pile of rubble where the painter's house was?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: Why would it collapse, all of a sudden?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: I didn't see her outside today... she might be buried under all that.

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: Go get help!

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: Painter! Are you down there? Can you hear me?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: What's going on? I came as soon as I heard. Why did the house collapse like that?

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Where's the painter? And that visitor who wanted his painting restored?

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: If you've got time to ask questions, you've got time to dig!

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: I brought help!

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: Did you see anything?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: No. What about you?

steps.name: Other Townsfolk
steps.text: (Shake heads in unison)

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Nothing, not even a body.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Did they leave?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: We went around the town on our way here. No one saw the painter.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: Hey, what's this?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: A painting?

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: It's totally unharmed after being buried under rubble for so long?

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: What's the painting of? I can't tell.

steps.name: Art Shop Owner
steps.text: All we can see is a corner, and it's all blue. Is it the sky? Or the...

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: Shh...

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: We'll know once we dig it out.

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: Whoa—!

steps.name: Worried Townsfolk
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Bold Townsfolk
steps.text: What the heck is this?!
A ball of slime clings to his palm, shimmering under the sun, and leaving sticky threads as he tries to pull his hand free of the canvas.
